prior_importants.description: A refused tell can only come from the operator's `pup conductor tell`. Worker idle notices reach the conductor through Claude Code's peer socket (`notify_when_idle`) and never call `tellConductor`. So the clock still starts at the first `pup status` / `pup ui` look, and an operator who only runs `pup status` sees nothing on the first look after hours of blockage.

findings.description: The only thing that clears `conductor/blocked-since` is a look that sees the box `empty`. Any later non-empty look picks up the old timestamp, however long ago it was written. If no look happens while the box is empty, two separate short non-empty spells count as one long blockage. The conductor then shows up in Needs-you as `blocked` straight away, with a wrong age. This breaks the ADR's promise that "an operator typing into the conductor ... never shows up". A successful `tellConductor` also leaves the clock in place even though it sees an empty box at the end.

The new `conductor` need renders as `<li class="need need-conductor">` (web-dashboard-overview.service.ts:306). The page stylesheet only gives the red left border to `.need.need-question, .need.need-blocked, .need.need-stalled`. NEED_ORDER puts `conductor` between `question` and `blocked`, so when a question, a blocked conductor and a blocked session are all present, `pup dashboard` shows two red-bordered rows with the conductor between them unmarked. It looks like a low-urgency pr-open row, which goes against decision 168's ranking, while the other three surfaces show it at its true rank. Fix: add `.need.need-conductor` to the selector on line 265.

The `needsYou` JSDoc still says "One line per session, its first reason in `NEED_ORDER`". The change adds a `conductor` line that belongs to no session; its `sessionId` is the window name `pup-conductor-<id>`. A reader of `needsYou` would not expect that line to be there. Suggested replacement: "One line per session (plus the conductor's, when blocked; decision 168), its first reason in `NEED_ORDER`".

The `DashboardSnapshot` JSDoc still says everything is "answered by the store and the events files" plus one capture of the conductor's pane. But building a snapshot now also creates or removes `conductor/blocked-since`, including from readers documented as read-only such as the web dashboard's GET. Add "and writes the blocked clock" to that sentence.

The `running ?` guard in `const blocked = running ? conductorBlock(repoPath, now) : undefined;` is redundant. `conductorBlock` already returns `undefined` when `conductorPane` finds no pane. `const blocked = conductorBlock(repoPath, now);` drops the ternary and costs at most one extra tmux probe on a stopped conductor.

process_issues.description: The validator confirmed the clock-merge important but suggested posting it as minor, because it cannot happen while `pup ui` or `pup dashboard` polls every 2s. The orchestrator kept it important: it is reachable in the one-shot-reader setup decision 168 targets, and it breaks the ADR's 'operator typing never shows up' promise.

The head SHA ce61e5a is the same one the prior record reviewed, so this was a re-ask on that head. The prior important at conductor.service.ts 394-398 is still unresolved, and reviewers were briefed not to re-raise it. I dropped one simplicity nit (folding noteConductorBox's rmSync into dropBlockedSince) because its reviewer recommended leaving it.

`bash scripts/adr-index.sh` was refused under the CI lock. The reviewer found ADRs by Glob/Grep and did not read testing.md, and it did not check whether ADRs 0083/0085 need an 'Amended by' line for 0168.
The reviewer did not read the new ADR 0168 and found no ADR-index format test. Its greps covered only *.test.ts, so a guard in another file type would be missed.
